sections.heading: Passwords Are the Locks Nobody Sees
paragraphs: The weakest link in personal and business security is almost always a predictable password. A [password-generator:strong password generator] replaces guessable phrases with high-entropy randomness.
Service breaches happen; your defense is unrepeatable passwords, unique per account.
ChooseTools generates passwords locally in your browser using cryptographic randomness — nothing is created or stored on any server.

sections.heading: Length Beats Complexity
paragraphs: Modern guidance favors length: every additional character multiplies combinations enormously.
A 16-character mixed password exhausts brute force effectively; shorter ones fail faster even with added symbols.
File the strength curve and let the generator produce long, comfortable-to-paste results.

sections.heading: Understanding How Attackers Guess Passwords
paragraphs: Attackers do not try every combination randomly; they work from dictionaries, leaked password lists and predictable patterns like dates and keyboard sequences.
This is why short but complex passwords fail: an 8-character string with one symbol still resembles patterns dictionaries already contain.
Long random strings defeat both dictionary attacks and pattern reasoning, which is why the generator emphasizes length as the primary lever.
Even a simple long phrase of random words provides dramatically more security than a short jumble of symbols.

sections.heading: Estimating Entropy in Plain Terms
paragraphs: Entropy measures how many guesses an attacker would need on average to find your password. Each additional character class and each added character increases that number multiplicatively.
A twelve-character password drawn only from lowercase letters is far weaker than a sixteen-character one including all four classes.
The strength indicator gives immediate feedback, turning the abstract concept of entropy into a simple visual check before you save the credential.
Choosing length first and then enabling the character sets you are comfortable using produces genuinely strong results.

sections.heading: Passphrases: Random Words Are Better Remembered
paragraphs: Random word combinations deliver very high entropy while remaining pronounceable and memorable.
Passphrase mode strings together uncommon words with separators — an ideal compromise for humans and post-it-free storage.
Use them for the accounts where typing frequency is higher.

sections.heading: Never Reuse: Every Account Gets a Fresh Key
paragraphs: Reused passwords chain breaches together: one leak credentially hands over everything.
Generate unique credentials per site and store them in a password manager; the generator makes uniqueness effortless.
Breach hygiene begins before hacking does.

sections.heading: Best Practices for Storing What You Generate
paragraphs: A password manager is the safest place for the credentials this tool generates, encrypting them behind a single master passphrase you remember.
Where a manager is not an option, store the generated values in encrypted notes rather than plain text files or spreadsheets.
Enable two-factor authentication on every account that offers it, so a stolen password alone is never enough to gain access.
Regularly replace passwords on critical accounts, especially email and banking, using the generator for each rotation.

sections.heading: When to Regenerate Passwords
paragraphs: Security teams recommend rotating passwords after any suspected breach, before and after travel on shared devices, and whenever a service reports an incident.
Passwords shared with someone else should be replaced immediately, since shared credentials travel to every account that ever used them.
Regeneration is also the right response to the ever-present risk of reused credentials found in public leak databases.
With the generator ready in a tab, each of these moments turns into a thirty-second task instead of an excuse to postpone.

sections.heading: Building a Personal Rotation Schedule
paragraphs: Security experts generally agree that urgent rotation matters more than fixed calendars, but a simple rhythm helps people stay current.
A practical pattern is reviewing critical accounts quarterly and replacing the unsaved, unmanaged ones monthly.
Tying rotation to recurring events, such as the first day of each quarter, turns the chore into a routine rather than a scramble.
Each rotation is a fresh click of generate and save, so the habit stays cheap enough to keep.

sections.heading: Cryptographically Local Randomness
paragraphs: Quality randomness comes from the operating system's crypto source through the browser's secure random API.
Generation happening locally means no transport, no logs and no server-side predictability.
Secure by construction, private by design.
